Appearance:
 Shri Sameer Kumar Shrivastava - Advocate for the petiti  Shri A. P. S. Tomar - Government Advocate for responden  Shri Pradeep Katare - Advocate for respondent No.2.

ORDER This is the first application filed by the applicant under Section 482 of the B.N.S.S. for grant of anticipatory bail relating to Crime No.111/2024 registered at Police Station Gohad, District Bhind (M.P.) for the offence under Sections 420, 379, 294, 120 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.

Brief facts of the case are that the respondent No.2, Pradeep Sharma filed a private complaint for lodging the criminal case against the present applicant and co-accused Man Singh, under Section 420, 379, 294, 120 of the IPC by stating that co-accused Man Singh has executed a sale deed dated 25.02.2021 of land bearing survey No. 379 measuring areas 0.27 hectare in favor of the respondent No.2.

Thereafter, the co-accused Man Singh made a second sale deed of the very same land in favor of present applicant on 26.05.2022, when the complainant opposed the same, then the co-accused Man Singh theft the crop of complainant's agricultural land and abused him.
Accordingly, a case has been registered against the present applicant.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-GWL:19781 2 MCRC-38984-2024
Learned counsel for the applicant contended that applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in this offence.
The applicant resided in United State from 2013 to 2020 and in the year 2022 only for making the sale deed, she visited Gohad (M.P.), therefore, she did no commit any forgery with the complainant.

sentences.text: present applicant, prior to making any sale deed, verified the mutation status of the disputed land bearing survey No. 379 on the official website of the Madhya Pradesh Land Record Authority and after duly verifying the same, she purchased the land in dispute.
She is the bonafide purchaser on the land in dispute.
Applicant has also filed a civil suit for declaration of title and permanent injunction.
Respondent No.2 has also filed a separate civil suit against her.
But, the fact of filing of civil suit was not disclosed by the respondent No.2 before the concerned Magistrate while filing the criminal case.
Arrest warrant has been issued against applicant.
Hence, learned counsel for applicant prays that the bail application allowed and applicant be granted anticipatory bail.

Per-contra, learned counsel for the respondent No.2 opposes the bail application and prays for its rejection by submitting that prima facie, sufficient evidence is available against the present applicant in respect of the aforesaid offence, therefore, he is not entitled to be released on anticipatory bail.
Learned counsel for respondent No.1/State submitted that the offence has been registered over a private complaint, therefore, State is not concerned with the matter.
Perused the impugned order of the trial Court as well as the case dairy.

Considering all the facts and circumstances of the case, arguments advanced by both the parties, nature of allegation and also taking note of the fact that the instant sale deed has been executed in the name of present applicant,
this Court is not inclined to grant anticipatory bail to this applicant.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-GWL:19781 3 MCRC-38984-2024
Hence, this first bail application filed by applicant under section 482 of B.N.S.S. is hereby dismissed.
Certified copy as per rules.
